title: Hat Ising universality
credit: Hat tiling: Smith, Myers, Kaplan, Goodman-Strauss (2023); numerics on hat-tiling Ising models as cited in the notes (arXiv:2402.11331, arXiv:2307.11054); background: Chelkak-Smirnov universality on isoradial graphs.
plain: Put an Ising magnet on each tile of a hat tiling, with neighbouring tiles interacting. Show that there is one critical temperature shared by all hat tilings, and that near it the magnetisation, susceptibility and correlation length follow the square-lattice laws with exponents 1/8, 7/4 and 1. Part (i) of QED-M148 (the common critical temperature) is the first step of both problems.
math: Let T be any hat tiling (tiling of ℂ by isometric copies, reflections allowed, of the Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss hat; all such tilings form the hull) and G its tile-adjacency graph (tiles sharing a boundary segment), with the J=1 ferromagnetic Ising model. Prove: there is β_c ∈ (0,∞), the same for all T, such that, with constants c, C, δ > 0 depending only on T: (a) the plus-state magnetization M_T(β,x) = 0 for all tiles x and 0 ≤ β ≤ β_c, and c(β−β_c)^{1/8} ≤ M_T(β,x) ≤ C(β−β_c)^{1/8} uniformly in x for β_c < β < β_c+δ; (b) for β_c−δ < β < β_c, χ_T(β) = sup_x Σ_y ⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β satisfies c(β_c−β)^{−7/4} ≤ χ_T(β) ≤ C(β_c−β)^{−7/4}; (c) for β_c−δ < β < β_c, the inverse correlation length 1/ξ_T(β) = liminf_{|x−y|→∞} (−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β/|x−y|) satisfies c(β_c−β) ≤ 1/ξ_T(β) ≤ C(β_c−β). Shared milestone: the existence of a common $\beta_c$ is also part (i) of QED-M148; it can be credited separately from the exponent bounds.
